items.definition: Very wicked or evil, often used about a secret plan to do harm.
items.example: Police uncovered a nefarious plot to defraud elderly investors.
items.definition_previous: Wicked or criminal.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: extremely wicked

items.definition: Seeming calm and not worried, as if nothing matters very much.
items.example: She gave a nonchalant shrug, though her heart was pounding.
items.picture_idea: A person shrugging calmly with hands in pockets
items.definition_previous: Calm and relaxed, as if not worried or interested.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: marked by blithe unconcern

items.definition: No longer used, because something newer and better has taken its place.
items.example: Floppy disks became obsolete once USB drives appeared.
items.picture_idea: A floppy disk next to a modern USB stick
items.definition_previous: No longer used because something newer has replaced it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: no longer in use

items.definition: Stubborn and not willing to change your mind, even when people ask you to.
items.example: The obstinate old farmer refused to sell his land at any price.
items.picture_idea: A person with folded arms shaking their head
items.definition_previous: Stubborn and refusing to change your mind.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield

items.definition: Given as the reason for something, but maybe not the real reason.
items.explanation: Usually used with 'reason' or 'purpose'; the related adverb is 'ostensibly'.
items.example: The ostensible purpose of the visit was a routine inspection.
items.definition_previous: Seeming or stated to be true, but perhaps not the real reason.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: represented or appearing as such; pretended

items.definition: Done with very great care and effort, paying attention to every small detail.
items.example: The restoration of the painting was a painstaking process that took years.
items.picture_idea: A restorer carefully cleaning a painting with a tiny brush
items.definition_previous: Done with great care and effort.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: characterized by extreme care and great effort

items.definition: Most important of all; more important than anything else.
items.example: The safety of the passengers is paramount.
items.definition_previous: More important than anything else.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: having superior power and influence
definition_basis.batch_note: The only WordNet sense given (superior power and influence) is a loose match for the 'most important' meaning.

items.definition: Spreading into every part of a place or thing, so that it is hard to avoid.
items.example: A pervasive smell of smoke hung over the town after the fire.
items.definition_previous: Spreading through every part of something and hard to avoid.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: spreading or spread throughout

items.definition: Dealing with things in a sensible way that works in real life.
items.example: The mayor took a pragmatic approach and fixed the roads before building the park.
items.definition_previous: Dealing with problems in a practical, realistic way.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: concerned with practical matters

items.definition: Not safe or steady, and likely to fall or go wrong.
items.example: The hikers made their way along a precarious ledge above the valley.
items.picture_idea: A boulder balanced on the edge of a cliff
items.definition_previous: Unsafe or likely to fall or fail.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: not secure; beset with difficulties

items.definition: Producing a lot of work, such as books, music or art.
items.example: She was a prolific author who wrote more than sixty novels.
items.picture_idea: A writer at a desk beside tall stacks of books
items.definition_previous: Producing a great deal of work or many results.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: intellectually productive

items.definition: A state of not knowing which choice to make in a hard situation.
items.example: He was in a quandary over whether to accept the job abroad or stay with his family.
items.picture_idea: A person standing at a fork in a road, unsure which way to go
items.definition_previous: A state of not knowing what to do in a difficult situation.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: state of uncertainty or perplexity especially as requiring a choice between equally unfavorable options

items.definition: Deep, bitter anger toward someone that lasts for a long time.
items.example: The two brothers argued without rancor, and they were friends again by dinner.
items.definition_previous: Deep, long-lasting bitterness and ill will.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will

items.definition: Stubbornly refusing to obey or be controlled by someone in charge.
items.example: The teacher struggled with a recalcitrant class that would not settle down.
items.definition_previous: Stubbornly refusing to obey rules or orders.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: stubbornly resistant to authority or control

items.definition: Not willing to talk much about your thoughts, feelings or private life.
items.example: He was reticent about his past and rarely mentioned his childhood.
items.definition_previous: Unwilling to speak freely about your thoughts or feelings.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: temperamentally disinclined to talk

items.definition: To look at something very closely and carefully, checking every small detail.
items.example: Auditors will scrutinize every page of the company's accounts.
items.picture_idea: A person studying a document through a magnifying glass
items.definition_previous: To examine something very closely and carefully.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: to look at critically or searchingly, or in minute detail

items.definition: Doubting that something is true, good or will work, and not easily convinced.
items.example: Scientists were skeptical of the miracle cure.
items.picture_idea: A person with a raised eyebrow and arms crossed
items.definition_previous: Doubting that something is true or will work.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: marked by or given to doubt

items.definition: The comfort you feel when you are sad or disappointed.
items.example: She found solace in music after her father died.
items.picture_idea: One person comforting another with a hug
items.definition_previous: Comfort felt in a time of sadness or disappointment.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the comfort you feel when consoled in times of disappointment

items.definition: Seeming true or real, but actually false or not valid.
items.example: The lawyer dismissed the claim as spurious and without evidence.
items.definition_previous: False or fake, though made to look real.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: ostensibly valid, but not actually valid

items.definition: Staying calm and not complaining when something painful or hard happens.
items.example: The stoic soldier endured the cold without a word of complaint.
items.definition_previous: Accepting pain or hardship calmly without complaining.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: seeming unaffected by pleasure or pain; impassive

items.definition: Holding on firmly to a goal and never giving up.
items.example: The tenacious reporter chased the story for three years.
items.definition_previous: Holding firmly to a goal and refusing to give up.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: stubbornly unyielding

items.definition: Not final or certain yet, and could still change.
items.example: The two sides reached a tentative agreement that still needs approval.
items.definition_previous: Not certain or final; done without full confidence.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: under terms not final or fully worked out or agreed upon

items.definition: A nervous feeling of fear or worry about something that may happen.
items.example: She opened the letter with trepidation.
items.definition_previous: A feeling of fear or worry about something that may happen.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a feeling of alarm or dread

items.definition: Seeming to be everywhere, or found in every place, all the time.
items.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.
items.definition_previous: Seeming to be found everywhere at once.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: being present everywhere at once

items.definition: To make something weaker little by little, often in a hidden way.
items.example: Constant criticism can undermine a child's confidence.
items.definition_previous: To weaken something slowly or secretly.

definition_basis.note: no WordNet meaning fit; written by Claude
definition_basis.batch_note: Neither WordNet meaning given (sabotage, or hollowing out ground) matches the 'weaken gradually' meaning used in our definition and example.

items.definition: Willing to lie, cheat, or do wrong things to get what you want.
items.example: Unscrupulous dealers sold fake tickets to eager fans.
items.definition_previous: Willing to do dishonest or unfair things to get what you want.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: without scruples or principles

items.definition: To take power or a position by force, without having the right to it.
items.example: The general tried to usurp the throne from the young king.
items.picture_idea: A figure snatching a crown from a king
items.definition_previous: To take a position or power by force or without the right to it.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: seize and take control without authority and possibly with force; take as one's right or possession

items.definition: To respect someone or something very deeply, often as wise or holy.
items.example: Many villagers venerate the old teacher as a wise guide.
items.definition_previous: To treat someone or something with deep respect.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe of

items.definition: To annoy or upset someone, often with small troubles that keep happening.
items.example: The endless delays vexed the travelers.
items.definition_previous: To annoy or trouble someone.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: cause annoyance in; disturb, especially by minor irritations

items.definition: To clear someone of blame; also, to show that a person or idea was right.
items.example: New evidence vindicated the man who had been accused of theft.
items.definition_previous: To clear someone of blame or show that they were right.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: clear of accusation, blame, suspicion, or doubt with supporting proof

items.definition: Very harsh and cruel in what is said or written.
items.example: The critic wrote a vitriolic review that left the actors in tears.
items.definition_previous: Full of bitter, cruel criticism.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: harsh or corrosive in tone

items.definition: Likely to change suddenly, or to turn violent.
items.example: Oil prices have been volatile this year.
items.definition_previous: Likely to change suddenly or become violent.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: liable to lead to sudden change or violence

items.definition: To slowly grow weaker, smaller, or less important.
items.explanation: Often used for the moon when it appears to shrink.
items.example: Public interest in the scandal began to wane after a few weeks.
items.picture_idea: The moon shrinking from full to a thin crescent
items.definition_previous: To slowly become weaker, smaller, or less important.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: grow smaller

items.definition: Careful and watchful because you think something may be dangerous or go wrong.
items.example: The dog was wary of strangers.
items.picture_idea: A cautious dog peering at a stranger
items.definition_previous: Careful because you think something may be dangerous.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: marked by keen caution and watchful prudence

items.definition: Playful and odd in a way that is charming or funny.
items.example: The garden was full of whimsical statues of frogs wearing hats.
items.picture_idea: A frog statue wearing a tiny hat in a garden
items.definition_previous: Playful and unusual in a charming way.

definition_basis.note: no WordNet meaning fit; written by Claude
definition_basis.batch_note: The only WordNet sense (random, impulsive, capricious) does not match our playful, charming meaning.

items.definition: Quietly sad as you think about something you miss or cannot have.
items.example: He gave a wistful smile as he looked at the old photographs.
items.picture_idea: A person smiling sadly while holding an old photograph
items.definition_previous: Feeling a quiet, sad longing for something in the past or out of reach.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: showing pensive sadness

items.definition: To stay strong against force, pressure, or damage without giving way.
items.example: The old bridge has withstood a hundred years of floods.
items.picture_idea: A stone bridge standing firm in a flood
items.definition_previous: To remain strong against pressure, force, or damage.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: resist or confront with resistance

items.definition: To want something very much, especially something you do not have or cannot be near.
items.example: Living in the city, she yearned for the quiet of the countryside.
items.picture_idea: A person gazing longingly out of a window
items.definition_previous: To want something very much, especially something far away or lost.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: have a desire for something or someone who is not present

items.definition: Very eager and full of energy for a cause or goal.
items.example: A zealous volunteer, he spent every weekend cleaning the river.
items.definition_previous: Full of great energy and enthusiasm for a cause.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: marked by active interest and enthusiasm

items.definition: The highest point of something, or the time when it is most successful.
items.example: The empire reached its zenith in the twelfth century.
items.picture_idea: The sun at its highest point in the sky
items.definition_previous: The highest point, or the time of greatest success.

definition_basis.note: no WordNet meaning fit; written by Claude
definition_basis.batch_note: The only WordNet sense is the astronomical point overhead; our meaning is the figurative 'highest point', which is not listed.

items.definition: Harmful in a slow, hidden way that is hard to notice at first.
items.example: Experts warned of the pernicious effects of misinformation on public trust.
items.definition_previous: Causing harm in a gradual, hidden way.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way

items.definition: Done quickly, with little care or interest, just to get it finished.
items.example: He gave the report a perfunctory glance and handed it back.
items.definition_previous: Done quickly and without real care or interest.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough

items.definition: So strong that you can almost feel or touch it.
items.example: There was a palpable sense of relief when the results were announced.
items.definition_previous: So strong that it can almost be felt or touched.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: so intense as to be almost touched or felt

items.definition: Giving a sign that something bad or dangerous will happen soon.
items.example: Ominous black clouds gathered over the harbor.
items.picture_idea: Dark storm clouds over a harbor
items.definition_previous: Suggesting that something bad is going to happen.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: threatening or foreshadowing evil or tragic developments

items.definition: Very, very hungry, as if you could eat a huge amount.
items.example: After the long hike, the children were ravenous.
items.picture_idea: A child eagerly eating a large plate of food
items.definition_previous: Extremely hungry.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: extremely hungry

items.definition: Happening now and then, at odd times, not in a regular pattern.
items.example: Sporadic gunfire was heard throughout the night.
items.definition_previous: Happening only now and then, not regularly.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: recurring in scattered and irregular or unpredictable instances

items.definition: Able to get better or recover quickly after something bad or hard happens.
items.example: The resilient community rebuilt its homes within a year of the flood.
items.picture_idea: A small plant growing back through a crack in concrete
items.definition_previous: Able to recover quickly after trouble or hardship.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: recovering readily from adversity, depression, or the like

items.definition: To firmly reject something as untrue or wrong and refuse to accept it.
items.example: The senator repudiated the rumors in a public statement.
items.definition_previous: To firmly reject something as untrue or unacceptable.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: reject as untrue, unfounded, or unjust

items.definition: To think about something deeply for a long time.
items.explanation: Also used for cows chewing cud.
items.example: He sat by the window and ruminated on the choices he had made.
items.picture_idea: A person sitting by a window, deep in thought
items.definition_previous: To think deeply and at length about something.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: reflect deeply on a subject

items.definition: Cheerful and hopeful, even when things look difficult.
items.example: Despite the setbacks, the coach remained sanguine about the team's chances.
items.definition_previous: Cheerful and hopeful, especially in a difficult situation.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: confidently optimistic and cheerful
